Chapter 4: Gaining Emotional Distance and Clarifying Priorities
Even when you’ve got plenty of options and you’re trying to fairly weigh all the evidence, emotions can still sneak in and mess with your judgment. Have you ever faced a tough choice and felt totally swept up by anxiety, excitement, or that nagging fear of making the wrong move? It’s so easy to get overwhelmed—sometimes you might jump into a decision impulsively, or just freeze and end up doing nothing at all.
So, how do you step back and see things more clearly? How do you figure out what really matters to you?
Let me share a strategy that’s helped a lot of people: try using time as your lens. There’s a simple method called the “10/10/10” framework. Basically, you ask yourself—how will I feel about this decision in ten minutes, in ten months, and in ten years? This approach helps you separate those intense, short-term emotions from what’s truly important over the long haul.
Imagine someone thinking about leaving a secure job for a new opportunity. In the heat of the moment, fear can feel overwhelming. But if they picture how they’ll look back on this choice in a few months or even years, it gets easier to focus on deeper goals—and that anxiety starts to lose its grip.
Another trick? Pretend you’re advising a friend who’s facing the same choice. Funny how we’re often much better at giving wise, objective advice to others than to ourselves, right? By picturing yourself as an outside advisor, you get a clearer, calmer view—one that isn’t so tangled up in personal worries or desires.
Now, let’s talk about clarifying what’s most important. When you’re stuck between competing options, try to name the core values or goals that really drive you. Imagine a parent choosing between a demanding job and more time with family. It helps to actually list out top priorities, then see how each choice stacks up. Sometimes, this simple exercise reveals which option truly lines up with what matters most—not just what feels urgent right now.
Here are a few practical ways to get some emotional distance and clarify your priorities:
First, pause before deciding. Take a break, sleep on it, or talk things over with someone who isn’t caught up in your situation.
Second, use the outsider’s view. Imagine how a neutral observer would look at your decision and what advice they might give.
And third, list your core values. Write down what matters most to you—your biggest goals or guiding principles—then compare each option against that list.
By creating just a little space between your immediate feelings and your final decision, you’re much more likely to make choices that are thoughtful—and that actually support your long-term well-being. You won’t get rid of feelings entirely, but you can make sure they don’t run the whole show.
